messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed routing + sampling mismatch when inspect-mode is on for canaries. Some requests from mobile routes are showing full payloads in ephemeral logs even though sampling=0.02. Is that expected?
kevin: @maya nope, not expected. Are those tenant-level overrides or admin tokens in play? Can you paste the route id and a short example?
sasha: Might be the inspect toggle bypassing the sampler. We debated allowing inspect to force-capture for SRE/CS, but it should still respect quotas.
maya: route id: projects/mobile/v1/generate. Happened during today's canary — ~120 captures in 5m despite low qps.
liz: We have two UX modes in Console: "inspect = force" vs "inspect = sampled". Ops hate surprise full captures. Maybe defaulting to force was a mistake. :grimacing: 
maya: For privacy we can't leak PII in forced captures w/o consent. What does the backend actually do today?
kevin: runtime currently has allow_force_capture=true for admin tokens. Canary infra was using admin tokens so it bypassed the sampler. ops-bot: deploy started commit f4b2e1 feature/inspect-force -> staging
ops-bot: deploy succeeded staging 2026-03-18T14:02:11Z :white_check_mark:
sasha: Proposal: change default to allow_force_capture=false; add an "inspect with approval" flow in Console that records approver, reason, TTL and shows consent checklist.
liz: Also add post-capture redaction: run deid heuristics + tenant allowlist. If deid fails, redact entire request body and log a HMAC fingerprint. That avoids storing raw PII.
maya: HMAC approach sounds good — store HMAC(email) not the email itself. Use tenant-scoped KMS so keys aren't shared. Example config: 
```yaml
routes:
  - id: projects/mobile/v1/generate
    sampling:
      fraction: 0.02
      mode: prefix-ttl
    inspect:
      force_capture: false
      require_approval: true
    redaction:
      strategy: hmac
      key_ref: tenant_kms://projects/123/keys/telemetry
```
kevin: Two notes: 1) HMAC needs KMS calls and latency/cost considerations; 2) customers sometimes want an unmasked capture to debug. We should support a temporary unmask with a strict audit trail + TTL.
sasha: UX: show an explicit cost estimate in the Console when enabling "force capture" so people don't accidentally blow the storage budget. :money_with_wings:
maya: Can we add a per-route quota guard that auto-disables force_capture when budget exceeded? That would stop canary spikes from leaking everything.
liz: Telemetry changes we need: force_capture_count, forced_capture_cost_estimate, redaction_failures, deid_confidence_score, hmac_fallback_count. Dashboards + alerts for unexpected spikes.
kevin: Also instrument per-tenant key-missing and fallback behavior (e.g., if key missing, redact body + emit audit event).
sasha: Agreed. Action items: runtime default flip (kevin), Console approval + cost UI (sasha), metrics + alerts (liz), docs + sampling-exempt path examples (maya). Target next sprint?
maya: I'll open the sampling-exempt path RFC and include an incident snippet + small repro. Will add unit tests for TTL and admin-token checks.
ops-bot: Created issue RI-4782: "Sampling/Inspect: default deny + approval flow" assigned to kevin, sasha, liz, maya
kevin: I'll draft the runtime PR today and include an integration test that simulates canary tokens. :thumbsup:
sasha: I'll mock up Console flows (approval modal + cost estimate) and post screenshots in #design next week.
liz: I'll add the new metrics to the infra bill dashboard and wire an alert for >10 forced captures/min across a tenant.
maya: Thanks — let's avoid another surprise. If we need an emergency rollback plan, suggest: 1) revoke admin tokens for canary 2) enable sampler hard cap 3) flip allow_force_capture flag.
kevin: +1. I'll include rollback docs in the PR.
sasha: small follow-up: do we want inspect captures to be retained longer for debug? That affects retention policy and compliance. Maybe keep them ephemeral (24h) unless approval states otherwise.
liz: Retention should be configurable per-tenant but default to 24h for forced captures. We'll add a retention field to the sampling config.
maya: Cool. I'll paste the incident log and a short repro in the RFC. End of thread.
